title: Information Technology Act, 2000 — Section 43A (Compensation for Failure to Protect Data)

content.overview: Section 43A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 provides that where a body corporate possessing, dealing or handling any sensitive personal data or information in a computer resource that it owns, controls or operates is negligent in implementing and maintaining reasonable security practices and procedures and thereby causes wrongful loss or wrongful gain to any person, such body corporate is liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the affected person. After the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, treat s. 43A as residual/concurrent and prefer DPDP where it applies; verify transitional position against official text.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Body corporate handling sensitive personal data? (2) Negligence in reasonable security practices? (3) Wrongful loss or gain caused? (4) DPDP primary path instead?
content.study:
s. 43A is civil compensation for security negligence regarding sensitive personal data. DPDP is now the primary digital personal data statute — flag residual analysis.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Body corporate duty
sections.body: Applies to a body corporate possessing, dealing or handling sensitive personal data or information in a computer resource it owns, controls or operates.

sections.heading: Negligence
sections.body: Negligence in implementing and maintaining reasonable security practices and procedures.

sections.heading: Causation and loss
sections.body: Such negligence causes wrongful loss or wrongful gain to any person — compensation payable to the affected person.

sections.heading: DPDP interface
sections.body: DPDP Act 2023 is the primary digital personal data regime; assess whether s. 43A remains applicable on the facts as residual law.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify body corporate, sensitive personal data, security failure, loss/gain; check DPDP overlap.

provisions.title: Compensation for failure to protect data

examples.title: Data breach from weak security
examples.body: A company fails to maintain reasonable security for customer sensitive personal data leading to leak and wrongful loss — s. 43A compensation claim, subject to DPDP residual analysis.

hypotheticals.question: Is s. 43A still the main data protection remedy after DPDP?
hypotheticals.analysis: DPDP is primary for digital personal data; s. 43A is analysed as residual/concurrent only after checking current law.

distinctions.title: s. 43A data security vs s. 43 computer wrongs
distinctions.left: Compensation for negligent failure to protect sensitive personal data.
distinctions.right: Compensation for listed unauthorised acts on computer resources.

misconceptions.correction: DPDP is the primary digital personal data statute; treat s. 43A as residual pending official transitional analysis.
